title: US FAA says it will phase out floppy disks from air traffic control by 2028
why_read: A concrete example of long-tail legacy technology still running critical infrastructure, interesting as a systems/maintenance story.
analysis: The FAA plans to finally retire floppy disks used in air traffic control systems by 2028, highlighting how deeply legacy hardware can become embedded in critical infrastructure. This is a recurring type of story that engineers find interesting because it illustrates the real-world difficulty of modernizing safety-critical systems. There's no deep technical content, but it offers a useful reminder about technical debt at scale. Moderate interest as a discussion-starter rather than a deep technical piece.
